title: Yardstick Works
one_liner: Builds a private benchmark of a company's real tasks so it can pick AI models and track progress.
speaker: Alex Wissner-Gross / Peter Diamandis
context: Alex and Peter say that if you want AI to optimize something you care about, you should build a benchmark for it. Dave adds that you don't need to be an expert, just find the experts and define success. Salim wants internal company benchmarks too.
customer: Mid-size companies (50–500 staff) in legal, finance, insurance and operations-heavy fields that are rolling out AI agents, plus vertical SaaS vendors that want a public eval for their niche
problem: Public leaderboards don't measure their own work: on GDPX, finance and legal tasks scored near zero. So they can't tell which model or agent to trust with their workflows, or whether a new release really helps.
revenue_model: Fixed-fee eval build, about $8k–$20k per suite, plus a re-run retainer of about $1.5k a month that re-scores every new model release (estimate)
why_now: New models ship very often, the hosts say most eval suites copy human job titles rather than real work, and they call well-built benchmarks scarce and valuable.
first_steps: Turn 20 tasks from one industry you know (e.g. insurance claim triage) into a scored rubric and run three models on it
Publish the mini-leaderboard on LinkedIn with a 'want this for your workflows?' call to action
Offer three companies a discounted pilot that converts 30 of their real tasks into a private eval
cost_to_start: About 2–3 weeks and under $500 in model/API spend for a first public mini-benchmark
competition: Eval platforms and AI consultancies sell eval tooling, but few build domain-specific private benchmarks done-for-you for mid-market firms
risks: Clients' data sensitivity limits what can be run on third-party models. Scoring open-ended work is hard to make reliable. Large eval vendors may move down-market.

tool.title: Rubric Forge
tool.one_liner: Turns a list of your real work tasks into a scored benchmark spec and a side-by-side scoring sheet.
tool.demo: The customer pastes 5–30 tasks they actually do, one per line, with a short 'what good looks like' note for each. The page builds a benchmark spec (task, inputs, pass criteria, weight), a blank scoring grid for up to four models, and a weighted total once they enter pass/partial/fail for each cell. With a pasted API key it can draft pass criteria; example mode ships a filled insurance-claims set.
tool.data_plan: Customer's own task list and scores. Optional AI drafting with a visitor-supplied key. A bundled example set is labelled as an example.
acceptance: Pasting 10 tasks one per line creates 10 rows in the spec table, each with editable pass-criteria and weight fields
Entering pass/partial/fail for each model in the grid updates a weighted score bar for each model immediately
With no API key, 'Load example' fills an insurance-claims benchmark and shows a visible 'Example data' badge
An 'Export' button downloads the spec and scores as a JSON or CSV file
On a 390px-wide screen the scoring grid scrolls sideways without the page breaking
